title: PITB cross-benchmark competitive frontier

governing_policy.baseline_provenance: Every external result is a dated, source-linked reference under the source's own task condition. It is not a PITB run.
governing_policy.comparison_rule: A superiority claim requires the same immutable task set, model version, source visibility, tools, agent scaffold, stopping policy, verifier, hardware class and resource ceiling. Report deviations as non-matched descriptive comparisons.
governing_policy.admission_rule: A proof result is counted only after exact task/source/goal binding, independent checker replay and the task-family-specific semantic gates. Unknown or unauthenticated evidence is quarantined, not scored as success.
governing_policy.uncertainty_rule: Preserve the task's dependency clusters. Use repository/file clustered resampling for SorryDB; source-group stratification for AutoformBench; PBT identity grouping for FVSpec; implementation/spec pair grouping for Aegis.
governing_policy.target_status: All targets below are preregistered engineering goals, not achieved PITB results.

benchmarks.name: SorryDB
benchmarks.task_unit: one open Prop-valued sorry at a pinned repository commit and Lean version

reference_results.condition: live SorryDB_2601 leaderboard snapshot; single attempt per task
fraction solved by at least one listed approach; this is an ensemble coverage reference, not one model

targets.comparison: at least +3.1 percentage points versus the 57.2% live single-system reference
at least +4.8 percentage points versus 63.2% listed-system union; same declared system-count and total budget

qualification_gates: Pin the exact SorryDB JSON Git blob, task IDs, repository commit, Lean version, path and coordinates.
Reproduce the source location, sorry span, elaborated Prop goal and project build; quarantine mismatched tasks without removing them from the denominator.
Require independent kernel replay, source-binding evidence, no sorryAx/new sorry delta, and semantic/vacuity/assumption gates for assurance-adjusted success.
Report the official task-held-out result separately from the project-disjoint five-fold result; the original 1,000-task split overlaps all 78 repositories in the full snapshot.
Use paired repository/file-cluster statistics, charge every retry, and report cost per assurance-qualified task.
benchmarks.comparability_boundary: The 57.2% and 63.2% figures belong to the live official leaderboard on the January 2026 1,000-task snapshot. They are not automatically comparable to other model or benchmark scores; system membership, source visibility, retries and budgets must be frozen for a new claim.

benchmarks.name: AutoformBench
benchmarks.task_unit: one complete advanced-mathematics formalization task; every required declaration/obligation must pass

targets.comparison: first integer result clearing +5 percentage points over 281/341
first integer result clearing +10 percentage points over 281/341
at least 20% lower cost with no more than 1 percentage point completion regression

qualification_gates: Use the exact 341-task manifest, clean-room workspaces and pinned Lean/Mathlib versions.
Score the complete task, not an isolated declaration; preserve infrastructure failure as a separate state.
Report source-present and source-free conditions separately; do not compare across them.
Report cost, tokens, turns and generated code size alongside completion.
Respect the upstream CC BY-NC 4.0 release and its evaluation/research-only, not-training designation; do not import source excerpts, gold solutions or traces into training.
benchmarks.comparability_boundary: AutoformBench is infrastructure-building formalization, not isolated sorry completion. The headline 82.4% is source-present; it must not be pooled with SorryDB Pass@1 or FVSpec Pass@k.

benchmarks.name: FVSpec
benchmarks.task_unit: one Lean challenge linked to a source Python property-based test and implementation

reference_results.system: reported baseline model mean on easy tasks
reference_results.condition: paper-reported average over Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT 5.4

reference_results.system: reported baseline model mean on hard tasks
reference_results.condition: paper-reported average over Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT 5.4

targets.comparison: +5 percentage points over the reported mean baseline
+5 percentage points over the reported mean baseline
100% of counted successes must retain a verified source test, implementation and spec correspondence receipt

qualification_gates: Group formalization variants by their originating PBT; multiple variants are not independent source tasks.
Independently inspect semantic correspondence between source PBT, Python implementation, Lean implementation and generated proposition.
Audit Python-specific semantics, exceptions, mutation, numeric behavior and generated inputs before admitting a spec.
Report easy and hard strata separately, plus repository/PBT-cluster uncertainty.
A Lean kernel proof does not by itself prove that the translated proposition captures the original PBT.
benchmarks.comparability_boundary: The paper's easy/hard averages are a baseline summary, not one model's Pass@1. Compare model-specific results under the same task variants, source visibility and proof budget.

benchmarks.name: Aegis
benchmarks.task_unit: one generated Lean specification over a frozen Rust implementation, with proof or refutation

targets.comparison: +7.3 percentage points over the reported 52.7% result at the same 30-minute budget
100% of scored successes must pass exact Rust source, Aeneas translation and Lean statement binding

qualification_gates: Pin Rust source, compiler, Aeneas translation, Lean environment and specification candidate IDs.
Keep implementation identity separate from generated specification identity.
Audit machine arithmetic, casts, overflow, failure behavior, loops, mutation and aliasing.
Score proof and valid refutation separately; do not count a refutation as a proof completion.
Use the same stratified 2,000-task cohort and 30-minute cap for direct baseline comparison.
benchmarks.comparability_boundary: Aegis is much harder than saturated competition-math sets and is about implementation-level software obligations. The 52.7% reference is a sample, not a full-11,533-spec result.

benchmarks.name: LeanGraphSearch / MathlibQR / MathlibMPR
benchmarks.task_unit: one retrieval query over a pinned Mathlib graph, with a separately annotated sufficient premise route

reference_results.condition: complete annotated proof-route premise coverage; LeanSearch v2 0.391
complete annotated proof-route premise coverage; LeanSearch v2 0.413

targets.comparison: strict positive paired gain in assurance-qualified exact-target completion or lower cost at non-inferior completion; recall alone is insufficient

qualification_gates: Use the exact query subsets, target environments, graph manifest and route annotations.
Bind each query to raw ranked IDs, filtered candidate pool, retriever/checkpoint/configuration and resource budget.
Treat retriever scores as uncalibrated unless calibrated on separate held-out data.
Measure useful-novel-premise rate, sufficient-route recall, antichain-route coverage and exact-target proof completion.
Run no-retrieval, BM25, LeanSearch v2, DAPS, LeanGraphSearch and PITB graph-union arms under equal downstream prover budgets.
benchmarks.comparability_boundary: Recall@100, route coverage and Pass@turn are different metrics. LeanGraphSearch's reported downstream results are from its own integrated prover loop; they do not establish a direct PITB gain.

benchmarks.name: CoCo-Prover
benchmarks.task_unit: one proof obligation in a multi-obligation function or repository proof graph

reference_results.metric: reported cost reduction versus strongest baseline
reference_results.condition: up to 30.9% on a benchmark/system cell; authors report best solve rate on each evaluated benchmark and up to 100% on two

targets.comparison: show a strict improvement in the area/coverage of the success-cost frontier on at least three of five benchmarks without lowering the fixed-budget solve rate
target at least 20% lower cost at a matched success rate, subject to a per-benchmark paired comparison

qualification_gates: Keep per-obligation and repository-level denominators distinct.
Count orchestration, failed probes, parallel work and verification in total cost.
Report wall time and monetary/token cost separately; parallel search may reduce wall time while increasing compute.
Compare under matched base model, tools, resource ceilings and stopping rules.
Retain the AND/OR graph and invocation receipts to explain routing decisions.
benchmarks.comparability_boundary: The 30.9% figure is a maximum reported cell, not a universal average. It cannot be used as a single threshold across all five benchmarks.

benchmarks.name: Formal benchmark specification and evaluation assurance
benchmarks.task_unit: one benchmark task plus its source/specification, split, verifier and result custody chain

reference_results.condition: audit of five Lean benchmark families and forks; includes counterexamples, vacuity and unsound axioms

targets.comparison: 100% of admitted tasks have exact source, statement, environment and verifier receipts
zero dropped, overwritten, deduplicated or quarantined tasks without a retained reason and denominator record
100% detection of the registered benchmark-integrity attack corpus, with no weakened controls

qualification_gates: Verify source-to-goal correspondence independently of Lean kernel success.
Audit vacuity, missing hypotheses, axiom/sorry leakage, nontermination/timeouts and evaluation harness exploits.
Maintain a blinded negative-control corpus and mutation-tested independent verifier.
Use exact task custody, split membership, retry accounting and immutable report inputs.
Publish defect counts separately from prover solve rate.
benchmarks.comparability_boundary: This is an assurance track, not a prover leaderboard. Finding rates from an audit sample are not estimates of global benchmark defect prevalence.

claims_not_allowed: Do not report a pooled PITB score across SorryDB, AutoformBench, FVSpec, Aegis and Mathlib retrieval.
Do not call the SorryDB_2601 task-held-out split project-disjoint; use the separately generated project-disjoint folds for that claim.
Do not treat kernel acceptance as proof that a benchmark specification matches its source-level intent.
Do not treat retrieved candidates, retrieval scores or proof-term references as sufficient routes or logically necessary premises.
Do not claim SOTA from a comparison with unmatched models, source access, scaffolds, tools, time budgets, cost accounting or stopping policies.
Do not use AutoformBench's source-free CC BY-NC 4.0 release as training data; respect third-party source licenses separately.
